title: Diaspora
description: The Visual Memory of the Circassian People

photos.title: The Adyghe School in Syria
photos.description: A 20th-century photograph from Qunaitra, Syria showing the Adyghe School. The school was established in 1932 and continued operating until 1942. It was the first Circassian elementary school in the diaspora where the entire curriculum was taught in the Circassian language except for Arabic language classes.

photos.title: Circassian soldiers standing trial
photos.description: A painting dating to 1851, from Bromberg, Poland, showing Circassian soldiers standing trial. In September 1850, ten Kabardian horsemen deserted Russian service in Warsaw and fled into Prussia, hoping eventually to return to the Caucasus via Turkey. A clash with Prussian authorities near Bromberg left several dead and the survivors imprisoned. Their trial attracted European attention and sympathy, but Prussia later extradited them to Russia, where they lost their ranks and noble status and were sentenced to hard labor or exile.

photos.title: Syrian president Ahmad Nami
photos.description: A 1925 photograph from Syria, featuring Ahmad Ibrahim Fakhri Nami (Damat Ahmet Nami). Ahmad was married to Aysha, the daughter of the Ottoman Sultan Abdul Hamid II. He was a prominent political figure who served as the second president of Syria and its fifth Prime Minister. He was referred to as "Damat" (Son in law in Turkish) because he was married to the daughter of the Ottoman Sultan.
